properties.name: FIELD REPORT (Alex, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-17): after the update, "many redundant things were removed from my repos' skills; many now use get_skill" — so the served-skills decision landed as designed — and what his repos still need is per-repo procedural know-how (reflow2 does no file I/O), a taxonomy decided once before bulk capture, and an incremental, resumable, region-scoped adopt with a frontier query and a deferred-derivation marker
properties.statement:
Alex, by email, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-17, from asking Claude why his repos still keep skills of their own beside reflow2. In his words, condensed:

"After update to latest version, many redundant things were removed from my repos' skills. Many now use the get-skill from the reflow2 mcp. The taxonomy lives as Decisions." — the measurement dec:skills-served (his own 2026-07-25 proposal) was waiting for: served skills replaced the copied ones, and the project-side residue is thin.

WHY SKILLS ARE STILL NEEDED, his three reasons: (1) "Repo nav know-how is per-project, per-repo procedural knowledge. reflow2 does no file I/O by design. The agent is storing information about how to navigate the repos" — import/resolver/test conventions. (2) "A vertical slice orchestration adopt doesn't do: adopt is breadth-first over an entire repo. It says it will report false gaps if done regionally." (3) A human-in-the-loop reviews artifacts. "After upgrade, these are thin project adapters, not competing playbooks."

WHAT HE ASKS FOR: (a) "a first-class way to teach the agent a repo's import/resolver/test conventions"; (b) "a golden-thread or region-scoped capture mode that doesn't trip the partial-graph gap problem"; (c) an `establish-taxonomy` skill "that runs early in adopt (or after genesis), notices you are about to model repeated instances of the same category, and drives you to author the encoding once as accepted Decisions before bulk capture, so every later capture cites them instead of re-deciding ad hoc. It's the missing bridge between genesis/adopt and 'how does this project represent its own recurring parts'. This exists as the master representation decision but nothing helps you write them"; (d) "reflow2 has no incremental, interactive, resumable capture mode" — the unique thing his skill does is "write through instead of accumulate-then-commit; the graph as worklist + memory + resume-state as an explicit contract; a typed structural-vs-intent gap with a findable deferral marker" — and he names the two primitives a native mode would need: "a frontier query and a deferred-derivation marker."

He offered to explain anything that does not make sense; nothing here was reworded beyond condensing.
